    Important Words
    • madhu-pateḥ — of the Lord of Madhu
      madhu (Mathurā / the demon Madhu) + pati (lord). Kṛṣṇa as conqueror of Madhu, lord of Mathurā. The queen calls Him by His Mathurā-Dvārakā name — pointed reminder that He left Vraja and married elsewhere; viraha is geographic.
    • praṇaya-avalokam — affectionate glance
      praṇaya (intimate love) + avaloka (glance). Praṇaya is one of the higher gradations of love in Rūpa Gosvāmī's taxonomy (Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu) — love with the freedom to behave casually, as among intimates. Its absence parches.
    • muṣṭa-hṛdayāḥ — whose hearts are stolen
      muṣṭa (stolen) + hṛdaya (heart). Bhagavān is hari — He steals hearts and gives them back as gifts only sometimes. The queens' hearts are gone; the rivers' hearts are gone; the lotuses' hearts are gone.
    • sindhu-patnyaḥ — wives of the ocean
      sindhu (ocean) + patnī (wife). Rivers personified as the ocean's wives. The queen finds a relational structure even in geography — every flow has a beloved, and every drying is a separation.
    • iṣṭa-bhartuḥ — of their dear husband
      iṣṭa (cherished) + bhartṛ (husband, supporter). The same vocabulary — bhartṛ — verse 27 uses of Kṛṣṇa as the queens' bhartṛ-buddhi (regarded-as-husband). The marriage frame holds throughout the songs.
    O rivers, wives of the ocean, your pools have now dried up. Alas, you have shriveled to nothing, and your wealth of lotuses has vanished. Are you, then, like us, who are withering away because of not receiving the affectionate glance of our dear husband, the Lord of Madhu, who has cheated our hearts?
    Purport

    During the summer the rivers do not receive downpours of water provided by their husband, the ocean, via the clouds. But the real reason for the rivers’ emaciation, as the queens see it, is that they have failed to obtain the loving glance of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the reservoir of all happiness.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O rivers, wives of the ocean, your pools have now dried up. Alas, you have shriveled to nothing, and your wealth of lotuses has vanished. Are you, then, like us, who are withering away because of not receiving the affectionate glance of our dear husband, the Lord of Madhu, who has cheated our hearts?
    Commentary

    "O wives of the ocean! O rivers! Your pools have all dried up. We will tell the cause. Similar to us who have not obtained the loving glance of the lord of the yadus, who is the giver of desired happiness even to you (istabhartuh), and who have thus become thin, with our hearts cheated, you also have been thin, with dried up pools and no beauty of lotuses."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Seeing the summer rivers with meager water, thinking the rivers have fainted, they speak among themselves about the rivers without even addressing the rivers, though they addressed the previous subjects. Bata expresses disappointment or lamentation. The wives of the ocean have lost their facial beauty because of no lotuses. Their hearts, the lakes, have dried up. Why? You do not receive the affectionate glance of your dear husband the ocean, because of separation in the form of summer. Ah! The rivers have become like us. Our faces have also withered. The word puru (abundant) indicates that they have become thin and have lost their facial beauty.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Seeing the rivers in the distance with lack of beauty because of meager water in the summer and no lotuses at night, the queens think the rivers are in great pain. Have you withered away because of not seeing your dear husband (īṣṭa-bhartuḥ)? Kṛṣna appeared in the Yadu dysnasty with all excellent to manifwst unlimited qualities. He should protect us also. But we do not even receive his affectionate glance. Or since he is the protector of the Yadus, he does not protect us. Not attaining his glance, we have lost our hearts (muṣṭa-hrḍayāḥ) and have become thinner than you. Hrāda (lake) sounds similar to hṛdaya (heart). Thus there is the suggestion that just as the lakes dry up in summer, the queen’s hearts have dried up. And as the rivers are devoid of the beauty of the lotus, so the lotus faces of the queens are devoid of beauty since they have withered. It is suggested also that they have become thin by wailing like the ocean and shedding tears like the cloud. The rivers also have great attachment to their husband, the ocean. Because of the ocean ignores them, they become thin.

    Important Words
    • haṁsa — swan
      The classical Vaiṣṇava bird — symbol of discrimination (separating milk from water), of the paramahaṁsa renunciate, and here pressed into service as Kṛṣṇa's secret messenger. The queen reads every haṁsa as His agent.
    • ajitaḥ — the unconquered one
      a + jita — unconquered. A name of Kṛṣṇa: no opponent has defeated Him. The queen's irony: He cannot be conquered, but His heart she expected to have conquered — and finds she has not.
    • cala-sauhṛdaḥ — of unsteady friendship
      cala (unsteady) + sauhṛda (friendship). The queen calls Bhagavān an unreliable friend. Gauḍīya commentators (Viśvanātha) gloss: this 'fault' is praise — only those whom He has bound by intimate love feel free to accuse Him so.
    • śriyam ṛte — without the goddess of fortune
      śrī (Lakṣmī) + ṛte (without). The chapter opened (90.1) with Kṛṣṇa as śriyaḥ patiḥ. Now the queen demands He come without Lakṣmī. Aiśvarya-saṅga is not what the lover wants; she wants the Person unaccompanied by His own opulence.
    • eka-niṣṭhā — exclusively devoted
      eka (one) + niṣṭhā (fixed devotion). The Gauḍīya keyword for ananyā-bhakti. The queen's stinging rhetorical question — 'is Lakṣmī the only eka-niṣṭhā?' — asserts the queens' own eka-niṣṭhā equally.
    • śaureḥ — of Śūra's descendant
      Genitive of Śauri — descendant of Śūrasena, an ancestor of Vasudeva. Kṛṣṇa named by His genealogical name. The queens claim Him in His full lineage, not as an abstract deity.
    Welcome, swan. Please sit here and drink some milk. Give us some news of the descendant of Śūra, dear one. We know you are His messenger. Is that invincible Lord doing well, and does that unreliable friend of ours still remember the words He spoke to us long ago? Why should we go and worship Him? O servant of a petty master, go tell Him who fulfills our desires to come here without the goddess of fortune. Is she the only woman exclusively devoted to Him?
    Purport

    Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī relates the following conversation between the queens and the swan: The queens ask, “Is the unconquerable Lord doing well?” The swan replies, “How can Lord Kṛṣṇa be doing well without you, His beloved consorts?” “But does He even remember what He once told one of us, Śrīmatī Rukmiṇī? Does He recall that He said, ‘In all My palaces I see no other wife as dear as you’?” “He does indeed remember this, and that is just why He sent me here. You should all go to Him and engage in His devotional service.” “Why should we go worship Him if He refuses to come here to be with us?” “But my dear oceans of compassion, He is suffering so much from your absence! How can He be saved from this distress?” “Just listen, O servant of a petty master: tell Him to come here, as He should. If He is suffering from lusty desires, He has only Himself to blame, since He Himself is the creator of Cupid’s power. We self-respecting ladies are not going to yield to His demand that we go seek Him out.” “So be it; then I will take my leave.” “No, one minute, dear swan. Ask Him to come to us here, but without the goddess of fortune, who always cheats us by keeping Him all to herself.” “Don’t you know that Goddess Lakṣmī is devoted exclusively to the Lord? How could He give her up like that?” “And is she the only woman in the world who is completely sold out to Him? What about us?”

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Welcome, swan. Please sit here and drink some milk. Give us some news of the descendant of Śūra, dear one. We know you are His messenger. Is that invincible Lord doing well, and does that unreliable friend of ours still remember the words He spoke to us long ago? Why should we go and worship Him? O servant of a petty master, go tell Him who fulfills our desires to come here without the goddess of fortune. Is she the only woman exclusively devoted to Him?
    Commentary

    Thinking that some swan is a messenger they speak. The swan send to say, "Indeed how can he be happy without you?" "Does he remember his loving words that he said previously such as ‘In all my palaces I see no other wife who is as loving as you (Rukmini)’ Being unwavering in his love, does he remember?" "He does remember, and sent me here. Go to him and worship him." "If he does remember, he is not responding to us. He does not even come here. Therefore, why should we worship him? Why should we go?" "But then how can he deliver you from the pain of longing?" "O fallen messenger(ksaudra)! You should call him here, the one who bestows pain through his love (kamadam). Let him come here! Because we are proud, we will not go to him." Thinking that the swan would agree and go and call him, they again spoke. "Cheating us, he enjoys with Laksmi alone. Call him here without Laksmi." "She is very attached to him alone. How is it possible to avoid her?" "Bring him without her. Among us women (striyam singular to represent a whole class), is she alone devoted to him and not us?" There is an alternate version : ksaudra alapam akamadam. The meaning is then "How can we worship him who has words like honey (ksaudram) and does not fulfill our desire for love? Why not here? Though she does not get his respect, let her continue to worship him, because we are proud women. Among women, we have our interested in our reputation and respect. "

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    With the arrival of morning, they think the swan is a messenger and speak to it. O swan! Have you arrived comfortably (svāgatam)? Or, it is splendid that you have come at this proper time. Please sit down. Drink some milk. Having welcomed the swan they then inquire. Please tell us! Aṅga indicates great respect. Or, it can indicate “You are part of our body.” This means “O intimate friend!” Tell us what our husband, who was born in the Śūra dynasty for everyone’s auspiciousness, is doing now. That is proper. We know for certain (nu) that you are his messenger. First they ask about his health. Is he, who cannot be controlled by anyone by love (ajitasya), happy (svasti)? This question shows some internal hatred. “O ladies! How can he be happy in separation from you?” Does he remember our answers to him when he tried to console us? Kiṁ vā (questions) can also be taken as kiṁvā (or). It indicates a question with a frown like kiṁ nu. Or, does he remember the answers he gave to us. “With gratitude he remembers you, since you are so devoted to him.” We do not believe that. He is unsteady in love (cala-sauhrdaḥ). “He is steady in love and desires you, who are most dear to him.” Proudly they answer, “Why should we serve him?” “He grants all desires, and thus should be worshipped.” Tell him to come without Lakṣmī. She alone is dedicated to him. This is statement uttered in great misery. They did not fear uttering the name of the father of their father-in-law (Śura) since the name takes a derivative form (śaureḥ).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    With the arrival of morning, they think the swan is a messenger and speak to it. O swan! Have you arrived comfortably (svāgatam)? Or, it is splendid that you have come at this proper time. Please sit down. Drink some milk. Having welcomed the swan, they then inquire. Please tell us! Aṅga indicates great respect. Or, it can indicate “You are part of our body.” This means “O intimate friend!” Tell us what our husband, who was born in the Śūra dynasty for everyone’s auspiciousness, is doing now. That is proper. We know for certain (nu) that you are his messenger. First they ask about his health. Is he, who cannot be controlled by anyone by love (ajitasya), happy (svasti)? This question shows some internal hatred. “O ladies! How can he be happy in separation from you?” Does he remember our answers to him when he tried to console us? Kiṁ vā (questions) can also be taken as kiṁvā (or). It indicates a question with a frown, like kiṁ nu. Or, does he remember the answers he gave to us? “With gratitude he remembers you, since you are so devoted to him.” We do not believe that. He is unsteady in love (cala-sauhrdaḥ). “He is steady in love and desires you, who are most dear to him.” Proudly they answer, “Why should we serve him?” “He grants all desires, and thus should be worshipped.” Tell him to come without Lakṣmī. She alone is dedicated to him” Or among all women she alone is dedicated to him alone. She is not fickle. This is stated with mockery. Giving up us queens, who are full dedicated to him, he serves Lakṣmī. Why should we worship him? Though the lord was directly present, they spoke in misery with the symptom called vaicittya, out of intense prema, as if he were absent. By this the Lord fell under their control. Though filled with pain of separaton, such conditions are the highest attainment. This is explained in Bhāgavatāmṛta.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    A swan walks up and a queen, half-mad, half-precise, recognizes Him as Kṛṣṇa's messenger and pours out her grievance: 'Tell that cheater to come without His Lakṣmī — is she the only one He admits?' The Bhāgavatam's loftiest verses include this acid theology: Kṛṣṇa's queens claim the right to wound Him with their words.

    Stories
    Uddhava the Yādava messenger to Vraja

    In SB 10.46-47 Kṛṣṇa sends Uddhava to console the gopīs of Vraja. They receive him with a similar mix of welcome and accusation — addressing a wandering bee instead of him, demanding to know if their cheater-Beloved still remembers them.

    The queen's outburst at 90.24 deliberately echoes that scene. Gauḍīyas read it as confirmation: the Dvārakā queens speak gopī-grammar. The 'invincible Lord' is teased; the 'unreliable friend' is named; Lakṣmī is dismissed. Only mādhurya-bhaktas dare such intimacy.

    Important Words
    • bhāvena — by the mood
      Instrumental of bhāva — mature emotional state on the way to prema. Rūpa Gosvāmī's middle stage in sādhana → bhāva → prema. The verse explicitly credits bhāva, not external practice, with delivering the queens to the goal.
    • yoga-īśvara-īśvare — the master of all masters of yoga
      Contiguous compound: yoga + īśvara + īśvare. Locative — directed toward Kṛṣṇa. He is yoga-īśvara-īśvara: master even of those who themselves master yoga. Bhakti reaches Him; yoga only approximates.
    • paramām gatim — the supreme destination
      param (supreme) + gati (destination). Not mokṣa understood as merging; in Gauḍīya reading, parama-gati is the spiritual world, eternal kṛṣṇa-sevā, the prayojana of Caitanya's siddhānta.
    • mādhavyaḥ — the wives of Mādhava
      From Mādhava (a name of Kṛṣṇa — husband of Lakṣmī / spring-lord). The queens are named relationally, by Him. Sambandha defines identity in Vaiṣṇava theology: who you are is whose you are.
    • lebhire — they attained
      Perfect of √labh — to obtain. The decisive verb. Not 'they tried' or 'they aspired' — they actually attained the highest destination. Bhāva-bhakti delivers; the chapter's psychological argument lands here.
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: By thus speaking and acting with such ecstatic love for Lord Kṛṣṇa, the master of all masters of mystic yoga, His loving wives attained the ultimate goal of life.
    Purport

    According to Ācārya Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī, here Śukadeva Gosvāmī uses the present tense of the word kriyamāṇena to indicate that the Lord’s queens attained His eternal abode immediately, without delay. By this insight the ācārya helps refute the false notion that after Lord Kṛṣṇa’s departure from this world, some primitive cowherds kidnapped His queens while they were under the protection of Arjuna. In fact, as the self-realized Vaiṣṇava commentators elsewhere explain, Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself appeared in the guise of the thieves who abducted the queens. For further information on this subject, see Śrīla Prabhupāda’s purport to Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 1.15.20 . Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī remarks that the supreme goal attained by these exalted women was not the liberation of the impersonal yogīs but the perfect state of prema-bhakti, pure loving devotion. Indeed, since they were already imbued with divine love of God from the very beginning, they possessed transcendental bodies of eternity, knowledge and bliss, in which they were fully able to relish the pleasure of reciprocating with the Supreme Lord in his most intimate, sweet pastimes. Specifically, in the opinion of Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī, their love of God matured into the ecstasy of madness in pure love ( bhāvonmada ), just as the gopīs’ love did when Kṛṣṇa disappeared from their midst during the rāsa dance. At that time the gopīs experienced the full development of ecstatic madness, which they expressed in their inquiries from the various creatures of the forest and in such words as kṛṣṇo ’haṁ paśyata gatim: “I am Kṛṣṇa! Just see how gracefully I move!” ( Bhāg. 10.30.19 ) Similarly, the vilāsa, or flourishing transformation, of the ecstatic love of Lord Dvārakādhīśa’s principal queens has produced the prema-vaicitrya symptoms they have exhibited here.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: By thus speaking and acting with such ecstatic love for Lord Kṛṣṇa, the master of all masters of mystic yoga, His loving wives attained the ultimate goal of life.
    Commentary

    "What goal did these women, possessing such love, for Krsna attain?" This verse answers. (It seems that in visvanatha’s version the last words are vaisnavim gatim, rather than paramam gatim, and thus his comments are upon the words vaisnavim gatim. ) They attained what is to be obtained by the vaisnavas, prema bhakti (vaisnavim gatim). But for those queens, who were beyond the material influence, purely spiritual entities, the most beloved eternal consorts of the Lord, endowed with sat cid ananda bodies, who relished the sweetness of the Lord rather than the taste of living in impersonal Brahman, the attainment could only be more intense prema, since it was impossible for them to attain liberation or any other such goal. Or "vaisnavi" can also mean "of visnu or of Krsna". Therefore vaisnavim gatim means that they attained the position (gatim) of Krsna, a state of oneness with Krsna, caused by the climax of madness in prema. The gopis of Vraja, after asking various questions when Krsna disappeared during the rasa dance, attained a state of identification with Krsna with the increase o their madness, thinking "I am Krsna. See my movements. Sb 10.30.19" In the same way, the queens, after asking questions to the osprey and others, attained that state of oneness. Attaining this state of oneness with Krsna and the prema vaicitrya exhibited by the queens is manifested at the stage of anuraga. This stage of anuraga attained by the queens is explained in the Ujjvala Nilamani.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Śukadeva now explains the greatness of the queens having such prema. By such mutual love as described, enacted for Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, the most rare to attain (yogeśvareśvare), the wives of Kṛṣṇa born in the Madhu dynasty attained the condition of Kṛṣṇa who spreads everywhere as Svayam Bhagavān (vaiṣṇavīm gatim). They become like him. Or, just as he is all pervading thay also become all pervading. Instead of vaiṣṇavīm sometimes paramām is seen. They attained a purely spiritual condition. The form kriyamānena (present) indicates that some of the queens after the defeat of Arjuna by the thieves (after Kṛṣṇa’s disappearance) had some obstacles, and attained another condition—in the material world (where they continued to serve). It is suitable that they attained the goal since it has been shown that they were the Lord’s svarūpa-śakti in relation to their marriage with him.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Śukadeva now explains the greatness of the queens having such prema, by which they controlled the Lord (iti). In the manner stated, by a similar bhāva, they attained the goal. This indicates the greatness of that bhāva. This love was directed to Kṛṣna, who attracts all hearts. But it is difficult to attain for others, since he is the Lord of all masters of yoga. With effort they can attain something, serving in the mind. And by his special śakti (yoga) he was able to enjoy with each one of the queens at the same time. This bhāva was continuous, not ever bringing full satisfaction (kriyamānena). They were the wives of he appeared in the Madhu dynasty (mādhavyaḥ). They attained a condition similar to his (gatim). Or they attained the state of highest pastimes. Each of them directly realized “Controlled by his devotee, he is enjoying with me alone at all times, in all ways. He never separates from me at any time for any reason.”

    Analogy

    Śukadeva calmly closes the song: the queens' madness was the highest reason. By speaking and feeling this way they reached the param gati — the same supreme destination austerities cannot guarantee. Vipralambha is itself a path; the queens' tears are the praxis.

    Stories
    Rūpa Gosvāmī's Vidagdha-mādhava

    Rūpa Gosvāmī's plays — Vidagdha-mādhava, Lalita-mādhava — exist precisely to systematize the rasa of these viraha-songs. He categorized the gopīs' and queens' utterances, their bhāvas, their physical signs, and demonstrated that vipralambha-rasa carries the devotee to the goal more swiftly than sambhoga-rasa.

    SB 90.25 is the verse Rūpa Gosvāmī's whole science rests on: 'by such feeling they attained the supreme destination.' Gauḍīya practice — rāgānugā-sādhana in the mood of separation — is the lived inheritance of this verse.

    Important Words
    • śruta-mātraḥ — merely heard about
      Contiguous compound: śruta (heard) + mātra (mere). The decisive Bhāgavata claim — hearing alone is enough. Śravaṇa is the first of bhakti's nine limbs (SB 7.5.23) and the foundation of all the others.
    • ākarṣate — He attracts
      Third singular of ā + √kṛṣ — to drag toward, attract. The same root that gives Kṛṣṇa His etymological gloss (kṛṣ + ṇa: 'the all-attractive'). Hearing about Him attracts because His name itself is attraction.
    • uru-gāya — He of wide-spreading songs
      uru (wide) + gāya (song, sung-about). A Vedic-style epithet — the Lord of vast renown, hymned everywhere. Bhāgavatam loves this register; here the chapter switches from queens' songs to phala-śruti's hymn-vocabulary.
    • manaḥ — mind
      The seat of bhakti or of viṣaya — whichever wins it owns the person. Verse 13 said the queens' dhī (intellect) was stolen; verse 26 generalizes: every woman's manaḥ is forcibly attracted. Bhakti is not gentle persuasion.
    • prasahya — forcibly
      Absolutive of pra + √sah — to overpower. Bhagavān's attraction is not optional. Gauḍīyas note: śaraṇāgati is the rational response to a pull one cannot resist anyway. Surrender is recognition, not addition.
    The Lord, whom countless songs glorify in countless ways, forcibly attracts the minds of all women who simply hear about Him. What to speak, then, of those women who see Him directly?
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Lord, whom countless songs glorify in countless ways, forcibly attracts the minds of all women who simply hear about Him. What to speak, then, of those women who see Him directly?
    Commentary

    Krsna, being glorified excellently by many songs, attracts the minds of women. But (va) what then to speak of those who see him?

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Now Śukadeva glorifies Kṛṣṇa. He who simply being heard, who is the subject of songs sung by many singers or many literary works or who is glorified profusely by singers or literary works, attracts the minds of women. What to speak of attracting the minds of women who see him. Another version has kutaḥ punaḥ instead of ca kim punaḥ. Thus the love of his wives with naturally great prema, who played with him always, was proper. One may hear other opinions, because even sages can be bewildered: ity aṅgopadiśanty eke vismṛtya prāg udāhṛtam muni-vāsa-nivāse kiṁ ghaṭetāriṣṭa-darśanam Some men proposed that the troubles were due to Akrūra’s absence, but they had forgotten the glories of the Supreme Lord, which they themselves had so often described. Indeed, how can calamities occur in a place where the Lord, the residence of all the sages, resides? SB 10.57.31

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Though only heard about, or only sung about profusely, he attracts the minds of women. What can one say how he attracts the mind of the women who directly see him. Developing attraction by hearing depends on concentration, but developing attraction by singing depends only a relationship, something lesser. That is the meaning of vā. Or singing plentifully with many songs attracts the mind. What can be said? And what then can be said of attaining the mind by seeing him? Singing is better than hearing but seeing is the best. This bhāva was suitable for the queens, who were most fortunate, always playing with the Lord.

    Anyone who merely hears about Kṛṣṇa has her mind seized; what then of those who saw Him face to face? The verse stages a sliding scale of bhakti's reach — śravaṇa is already total absorption, darśana is irresistible.

    Stories
    Parīkṣit hearing Bhāgavatam from Śuka

    Parīkṣit Mahārāja, with seven days to live, heard Bhāgavatam from Śukadeva — not seeing Kṛṣṇa, only hearing about Him. By śravaṇa alone he attained perfection (SB 12.6.7). Śuka himself, who was a brahman-realized renunciate, was drawn into Kṛṣṇa's mādhurya by hearing.

    Verse 90.26 makes this Bhāgavata's central wager: śravaṇa alone is sufficient. Gauḍīyas anchor saṅkīrtana on this verse — even those who never saw Kṛṣṇa are taken by hearing about Him. Vaiṣṇava aural transmission is empirically validated by Parīkṣit's own death-in-rapture.

    Important Words
    • jagat-gurum — the spiritual master of the universe
      jagat (universe) + guru (teacher). Bhagavān is the original guru — Brahmā received the Veda from Him (Bhāgavata 1.1.1). Yet the queens render Him pāda-saṁvāhana — they massage the universal teacher's feet. Reversal is bhakti's signature.
    • pāda-saṁvāhana — massaging the feet
      Compound: pāda (foot) + saṁvāhana (rubbing, massaging). The intimate service of a wife to a husband in classical dharma-śāstra — and the gopīs' own desired service (SB 10.31.13). The queens occupy this exact posture.
    • premṇā — with love
      Instrumental of prema — mature, supreme love. Distinguished by Rūpa Gosvāmī from rati and bhāva: prema is fully ripened, irreducible, the prayojana itself. The queens served with prema, not merely duty.
    • bhartṛ-buddhyā — thinking of Him as their husband
      Compound instrumental: bhartṛ (husband) + buddhi (conviction, conception). The queens know what they are doing. Sambandha is a buddhi — a settled cognition — not merely a feeling. The queens' theology is conscious.
    • tapaḥ — austerity
      From √tap. The verse asks: what tapas did they do to earn this? Gauḍīyas: tapas alone cannot earn it; only bhakti can, and only by Kṛṣṇa's grace. The queens have done both — uncountable austerity and pure-hearted bhakti.
    And how could one possibly describe the great austerities that had been performed by the women who perfectly served Him, the spiritual master of the universe, in pure ecstatic love? Thinking of Him as their husband, they rendered such intimate services as massaging His feet.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    And how could one possibly describe the great austerities that had been performed by the women who perfectly served Him, the spiritual master of the universe, in pure ecstatic love? Thinking of Him as their husband, they rendered such intimate services as massaging His feet.
    Commentary

    "What type of austerity is to be described for them for attaining that position?" "None, because they were nitya siddhas." Or one may ask, "For those among them who were sadhana siddhas, what type of austerities should have been done to get that position?" "They served him by massaging his feet, thinking of him as their husband."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    These women were most fortunate and not others because of their special love. Others just by thinking of him as their husband, though he was not their husband directly, because of prema, served the Supreme Lord (jagadguru) with complete devotion (sam—paryacaran) by meditating that they massaged his feet. How can one describe the greatness of their worship (tapas)? One cannot describe it. What to speak of describing those who directly serve him eternally as his wives?

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    They and no others are the most fortunate. They serve him with complete dedication, not depending on anything else--massaging his feet, washing his feet, combing his hair, fanning him etc. He is the most worthy of worship among all beings such as Brahmā. He is most rare to attain. They serve him, thinking of him as their husband (bhartṛ-buddhyā). How to describe the fortune of their worship? One cannot describe its greateness. Śukadeva indicates the mood of the gopīs. Though that is the highest prema, he gives respect to the queens’ love for Kṛṣṇa as a husband, in which they can freely serve him, and he is not satisfied with having marriage of the gopīs in Vraja. Thus here the greatness of the Lord accepting household life to enjoy various pastimes with the queens has been described. Or what can be said? He gave these dear devotees his mercy. That is the intention of the verse.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    The queens served the jagad-guru Himself — massaging the feet of Bhagavān, with the intimacy of wives. What tapas did they perform to earn this? The verse declines to count. Some prema is beyond accounting; it is given, not earned.

    Stories
    The gopīs' worship of Kātyāyanī

    Earlier in this canto (SB 10.22) the unmarried gopīs of Vraja vowed a month-long Kātyāyanī-vrata, bathing in the cold Yamunā daily and praying for Kṛṣṇa as husband. The vrata was intense, and Bhagavān answered by stealing their clothes and granting them what they asked.

    The queens of Dvārakā are similarly the fruit of tapas immeasurable. Gauḍīyas read the gopīs' vrata as the prototype: the queens have done its equivalent in past lives. The verse refuses to enumerate — only Bhagavān knows what His own devotees performed to earn His feet.

    Important Words
    • veda-uditam — enunciated in the Vedas
      Compound: veda + udita (spoken). Bhagavān, the source of the Veda, models obedience to it. Gauḍīyas: pravartaka of dharma submits to dharma's letter — the supreme legislator under His own law (Gītā 4.7-8).
    • gṛham — home
      Sanskrit for household. The gṛhastha-āśrama. Kṛṣṇa is shown here as the supreme gṛhastha — proof that household life, properly ordered toward Bhagavān, is no obstacle to the goal. Caitanya Mahāprabhu's gṛhastha disciples (Rāmānanda Rāya, Śivānanda Sena) inherited this image.
    • dharma-artha-kāmānām — of religiosity, prosperity and regulated desire
      The standard tri-varga (three goals of life, dharma + artha + kāma). Gauḍīyas: even when achieved, the tri-varga is not the goal — mokṣa and beyond it prema is. But achieving them rightly is the gṛhastha's foundation; the chapter shows Kṛṣṇa modeling it.
    • satām gatiḥ — the goal of saintly devotees
      satām (of the good, the sādhus) + gati (destination). A Bhāgavatam epithet for Kṛṣṇa: He Himself is the gati. The puruṣārtha and its giver are one. Caitanya-caritāmṛta: 'kṛṣṇa-prāpti — sei param-puruṣārtha.'
    • padam — the standard, the path
      Sanskrit pada — foot, footprint, standard. Kṛṣṇa repeatedly demonstrated (ādarśayat muhuḥ) the standard. Acārya-līlā: Bhagavān instructs by being, not only by speaking. The Veda is His act before it is His word.
    Thus observing the principles of duty enunciated in the Vedas, Lord Kṛṣṇa, the goal of the saintly devotees, repeatedly demonstrated how one can achieve at home the objectives of religiosity, economic development and regulated sense gratification.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Thus observing the principles of duty enunciated in the Vedas, Lord Kṛṣṇa, the goal of the saintly devotees, repeatedly demonstrated how one can achieve at home the objectives of religiosity, economic development and regulated sense gratification.
    Commentary

    He showed the house to be the place (padam) for achieving dharma artha and kama.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Having described Kṛṣṇa’s activities which clearly display his pastime nature, Śukadeva now describes how he gave happiness to all by being absorbed in Vedic dharma. He is the shelter of devotees absorbed in his pastimes constantly engaged in dharma like sacrifices prescribed by the Vedas. He showed the household goals of dharma, artha and kāma. He taught this to others since he is also the shelter of persons dedicate to dharma as well as of persons absorbed in his pastimes.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Though fixed in dharma, he delivered others by teaching dharma through his own conduct. In the way described, he performed dharma prescribed in the Vedas. He was the goal of the devotees, delivering bhakti by his mercy to the devotees. Or he was the goal for persons dedicated to dharma. By this he was to be attained by them. Or the goal was to give happiness to his devotees. He constantly performed dharma and constantly showed the goals (muhuḥ). This is to emphasize showing dharma.

    Important Words
    • gṛha-medhinām — of householders
      Compound: gṛha (home) + medhin (one who sacrifices). The gṛha-medhī is the householder who maintains domestic fire and sacrifices. Bhāgavatam distinguishes gṛha-medhī (attached) from gṛhastha (dutiful) — Kṛṣṇa demonstrates the dharmic ideal of the latter.
    • param dharmam — the highest religious principle
      param (highest) + dharma. Gauḍīyas: Bhagavata-dharma is param dharmam (SB 1.2.6: sa vai puṁsāṁ paro dharmo yato bhaktir adhokṣaje). The verse names what Kṛṣṇa enacted as param dharmam — making household life a vehicle of bhakti.
    • mahiṣyaḥ — queens
      Plural of mahiṣī — chief wife, queen. The technical term for a king's consecrated wife. All sixteen thousand were not concubines but mahiṣīs — wives in the full Vedic sense. Kṛṣṇa's householderhood is not metaphorical.
    • āsthitasya — of one situated in
      Genitive present participle of ā + √sthā. Kṛṣṇa is āsthita — established — in param dharma. Bhagavān's dharma-position is not a performance but a fixed location, His ontological standing.
    While fulfilling the highest standards of religious householder life, Lord Kṛṣṇa maintained more than 16,100 wives.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    While fulfilling the highest standards of religious householder life, Lord Kṛṣṇa maintained more than 16,100 wives.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    After having described the glories of the Yādavas with all the Lord’s sons when he became a householder, he now repeats this. He was situated in the most excellent (param) dharma of the householder since he is the shelter of all āśramas. It is also said: bhikṣābhujāc ca ye kecit parivrāṅ brahmacāriṇaḥ te py atraiva pratiṣṭhante gārhasthayaṁ tena cai varam Those who are sannyāsis, vanaprasthas, and brahmacārīs are all dependent upon the gṛhasthāśrama. Thus it is the best. Viṣṇu Purāṇa Or this was the best dharma because through it he could chiefly implement his goals. He was Svayam Bhagavān, who appeared in order to display his unlimited powers. Or, he attracted everyone’s heart (kṛṣṇasya) by the sweetness of performing those dharmas. Instead of ca sometimes tu is seen. This makes some distinction. He had eight principal queens (mentioned in the next verse) and he had sixteen thousand one hundred other queens.

    Important Words
    • rukmiṇī-pramukhāḥ — headed by Rukmiṇī
      Compound: rukmiṇī + pramukha (chief). Rukmiṇī is named pramukhā — first among the eight chief queens (also Satyabhāmā, Jāmbavatī, Kālindī, Mitravindā, Satyā, Bhadrā, Lakṣmaṇā). She is Lakṣmī Herself in Dvārakā-form.
    • strī-ratna-bhūtānām — of those who were woman-jewels
      Compound: strī (woman) + ratna (jewel) + bhūta (being). Bhāgavatam's vocabulary: certain women are ratna — jewels, irreplaceable. Gauḍīyas note: His chief queens are aṁśas of His own internal śakti, not material souls elevated.
    • anupūrvaśaḥ — one after another
      Adverbial from anupūrva — in proper sequence. The Bhāgavatam pays attention to order; the queens are not generic but each in her place. Vaiṣṇava theology of personhood: every devotee occupies a non-substitutable position.
    • putrāḥ — sons
      Plural of putra. Each queen has her own line. Gauḍīyas: Kṛṣṇa's family is real, His descendants real (the Yadu line ends not from non-existence but from His will, recorded in canto 11). Aiśvarya-līlā has full genealogical density.

    Related values & verses
    Concepts
    Jiva
    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    Among sixteen thousand wives, eight queens stand out as strī-ratna — woman-jewels — and Rukmiṇī is named first. Bhāgavatam refuses to dissolve the queens into a cloud; each one is named, distinguished, sons enumerated.

    Stories
    Rukmiṇī's letter to Kṛṣṇa

    Earlier in this canto (SB 10.52) Rukmiṇī, princess of Vidarbha, sent a brāhmaṇa with a letter to Kṛṣṇa pleading Him to abduct her from a forced marriage to Śiśupāla. Kṛṣṇa came, took her on His chariot, and made her chief queen of Dvārakā.

    Verse 90.30 names Rukmiṇī first among the eight strī-ratnas. Gauḍīyas treat her as the Dvārakā-side parallel of Vraja's Rādhā — chief consort, but in the aiśvarya register. Her recorded letter is one of Bhāgavatam's great prayer-texts.

    Important Words
    • amogha-gatiḥ — of unfailing power
      Contiguous compound: amogha (unfailing) + gati (course, effort). A divine epithet — His gati is amogha. Compare Bhagavad-gītā 9.31: na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati — His devotee's progress is also amogha. The grace and the giver share the same predicate.
    • īśvaraḥ — the Supreme Controller
      From √īś. Repeating from verse 15 — there in the queens' lament, here in Śuka's exposition. The same Bhagavān whose absence the queens felt is the īśvara whose every act succeeds.
    • ajījanat — He begot
      Reduplicated aorist of √jan — to generate. Bhagavān, who is aja (unborn), does janayati — He generates. The unborn one becomes the source of all generation: Gauḍīyas note this is svarūpa-śakti's playful contradiction.
    • ātma-jān — sons
      Compound: ātma (self) + ja (born of). 'Self-born' — born of one's own body. The technical Sanskrit term for natural-born children. Gauḍīyas note: Kṛṣṇa's sons are ātma-ja, His own — not vibhūti expansions but genuine progeny.
    • bhāryāḥ — wives
      Plural of bhāryā — that which must be maintained. The classical term for wife in dharma-śāstra. Bhāryā implies bharaṇa — full maintenance. Kṛṣṇa as supreme bharta supports them all without distinction.
    The Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose endeavor never fails, begot ten sons in each of His many wives.
    Purport

    The total number of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s sons was thus 161,080, and He also had a daughter by each wife.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose endeavor never fails, begot ten sons in each of His many wives.
    Commentary

    There is an alternate version amogha rati instead of amogha gatih. In that case the meaning is "one whose desires do not go in vain, whose desires are always fulfilled."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    These are recalled. In all the wives he had ten sons each, who were just like him since his intentions never go in vain. He begot in his wives, at the time they should appear, by his will, ten sons who were the abodes of the highest spiritual elements, since he was the Lord. Since he was the Lord this was not astonishing.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    These are recalled. In all the wives he had ten sons each, who were just like him since his pastimes never go in vain (amogha), because he was directly bhagavān (īśvaraḥ). Or “How was it possible to produce the same number of sons in each queen?” He is capable of everything (īśvaraḥ).

    Important Words
    • mahā-rathāḥ — great chariot-warriors
      Compound: mahā (great) + ratha (chariot). The Mahābhārata's technical rank: a warrior capable of fighting eleven thousand archers single-handed (atiratha is higher still). Bhagavān's sons fill this rank; aiśvarya extends through them.
    • uddāma-vīryāṇām — of unlimited valor
      Compound: uddāma (unrestrained) + vīrya (potency). Bhagavān's potency flows undammed through His progeny. Brahma-saṁhitā 5.46 — His expansions retain His power. The mahā-rathas are extensions of Kṛṣṇa's vīrya.
    • udāra-yaśasaḥ — of magnanimous fame
      udāra (generous, exalted) + yaśas (renown). Their fame is open-handed — distributed widely. The Yadu line's renown is itself a missionary fact in the world; Kṛṣṇa's family glorifies bhakti by existing.
    Among these sons, all possessing unlimited valor, eighteen were mahā-rathas of great renown. Now hear their names from me.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Among these sons, all possessing unlimited valor, eighteen were mahā-rathas of great renown. Now hear their names from me.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Though all the sons had great power, eighteen were special among them, having great strength and prowess (mahā-rathāḥ). Therefore they had great fame (udāra-yaśasas). Or, they were the best in courageous acts and also generous in performing rites (udāra-yaśasas). Hear of them from me. Others give them different names. Because of being discerned as the best, I will tell their names.

    Important Words
    • pradyumnaḥ — Pradyumna
      Rukmiṇī's son, the first among the eighteen mahā-rathas. Gauḍīyas identify him as Kāmadeva returned — and in Pañcarātra theology he is one of Bhagavān's catur-vyūha expansions (Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha). His name carries deity-level weight.
    • aniruddhaḥ — Aniruddha
      Pradyumna's son, Rukmavatī's grandson. Also a catur-vyūha-mūrti. Aniruddha means 'unobstructed.' Gauḍīya theology (Jīva Gosvāmī, Bhagavat-sandarbha) reads the catur-vyūha as Bhagavān's expansions for cosmic functions.
    • sāmbaḥ — Sāmba
      Son of Jāmbavatī. He plays a central — and unflattering — role in canto 11's account of the Yadu dynasty's end (he pretends to be a pregnant woman, gets cursed by sages, generates the club that destroys the Yadus). The naming here foreshadows that finale.
    • kaviḥ — Kavi (the wise one)
      Sanskrit for poet/seer. One of Kṛṣṇa's sons bears the name kavi — fitting for a dynasty in which 38 million teachers (verse 41) educated the children. Names declare destinies in Sanskrit genealogies.
    They were Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Dīptimān, Bhānu, Sāmba, Madhu, Bṛhadbhānu, Citrabhānu, Vṛka, Aruṇa, Puṣkara, Vedabāhu, Śrutadeva, Sunandana, Citrabāhu, Virūpa, Kavi and Nyagrodha.
    Purport

    In the opinion of Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī, the Aniruddha mentioned here is Lord Kṛṣṇa’s son, not His well-known grandson through Pradyumna.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    They were Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Dīptimān, Bhānu, Sāmba, Madhu, Bṛhadbhānu, Citrabhānu, Vṛka, Aruṇa, Puṣkara, Vedabāhu, Śrutadeva, Sunandana, Citrabāhu, Virūpa, Kavi and Nyagrodha.
    Commentary

    The Aniruddha listed here is a son of Krsna not the son of Pradyumna, as the subject is the sons of Krsna.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Many of these were mentioned in the Chapter Sixty-one. Dīptimāṁs tāmrataptādyā rohiṇyās tanayā hareḥ: Dīptimāna and Tāmrataptā were sons of Rohiṇī (chief of the sixteen thousand queens). (SB 10.61.18) Those listed here are the chief sons among the other queens. Instead of Citrabāhu sometimes Citrabarhi is seen and instead of Virūpa sometimes Virūtha is seen.

    Important Words
    • madhu-dviṣaḥ — of the enemy of Madhu
      Compound genitive: madhu (the demon Madhu) + dviṣ (enemy). Kṛṣṇa as Madhu's slayer. A name of Bhagavān fitted to the genealogical frame — the demon-slayer's son inherits the function.
    • pitṛvat — just like his father
      From pitṛ (father) + vat (suffix of likeness). The ultimate compliment in Sanskrit family-poetics. Pradyumna is Kṛṣṇa-pratīka — Kṛṣṇa-like in form, in valor, in glance. Gauḍīyas treat him as Kṛṣṇa's intimate aṁśa.
    • rukmiṇī-sutaḥ — son of Rukmiṇī
      Compound: rukmiṇī + suta. The chief queen's son inherits primacy. Vaiṣṇava sequence: Rukmiṇī (Lakṣmī) — Pradyumna (Kāma reborn) — Aniruddha (vyūha-Aniruddha). The Pañcarātra ladder appears inside the family.
    • prathamaḥ — the foremost
      Sanskrit for 'first.' Among the eighteen mahā-rathas Pradyumna is named first — formally his rank, and in resemblance to Kṛṣṇa, his honor. Birth-order tracks devotional proximity here.
    O best of kings, of these sons begotten by Lord Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Madhu, the most prominent was Rukmiṇī’s son Pradyumna. He was just like His father.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O best of kings, of these sons begotten by Lord Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Madhu, the most prominent was Rukmiṇī's son Pradyumna. He was just like His father.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Like their father the sons had great prowess. That is suggested by the name madhu-dviṣaḥ. Among them the best (prathamaḥ) was Pradyumna since he was equal to his father, being the son of Rukmiṇī, who was the best queen. O king of kings! You should understand this since you are famous in the family of kings.

    Related values & verses
    Concepts
    Jiva
    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    Pradyumna stands first — like his father in every feature. The son who most resembles Kṛṣṇa is the son named first. In Vaiṣṇava reckoning, likeness to Bhagavān is the primary distinction; everything else ranks beneath.

    Stories
    Pradyumna's birth and recovery from Śambara

    Earlier in this canto (SB 10.55) the demon Śambara, knowing the prophecy that Kṛṣṇa's son would kill him, stole the newborn Pradyumna and threw him into the sea. A great fish swallowed him; fishermen caught the fish and brought it to Śambara's kitchen, where Māyāvatī (Ratī, Kāmadeva's wife) raised him. Grown, Pradyumna killed Śambara and returned to Dvārakā.

    Verse 90.35 calls him pitṛvat — just like his father. Gauḍīyas note: his story rhymes with Kṛṣṇa's own (separation from parents at birth, demon-slaying, return). Even Bhagavān's progeny enacts His pattern.

    Important Words
    • nāga-ayuta-bala-anvitaḥ — endowed with the strength of ten thousand elephants
      Compound: nāga (elephant) + ayuta (ten thousand) + bala (strength) + anvita (endowed). Sanskrit's heroic measure. Aniruddha — etymologically 'unobstructable' — possesses ten thousand elephants' force. The name and the capacity match.
    • mahā-rathaḥ — the great chariot-warrior
      Compound: mahā + ratha. Pradyumna inherits this rank and his son Aniruddha exceeds it. Gauḍīya pattern: descent of svarūpa-śakti through Vaiṣṇava lineage is not metaphor — it is genealogical.
    • rukmiṇaḥ — of Rukmī
      Genitive of Rukmī — Rukmiṇī's brother, originally opposed to Kṛṣṇa (he tried to prevent his sister's marriage). His daughter Rukmavatī marries Pradyumna — old enmity dissolved in the next generation. Gauḍīya: bhakti unwinds family feuds.
    • duhitaram — the daughter
      Accusative of duhitṛ — daughter. Sanskrit's PIE-cognate word (cf. Greek thugatēr, English daughter). The Rukmī-Rukmiṇī-Pradyumna-Aniruddha cross-marriage knits the families that once warred — Bhagavān's līlā reconciles.
    The great warrior Pradyumna married Rukmī’s daughter [Rukmavatī], who gave birth to Aniruddha. He was as strong as ten thousand elephants.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The great warrior Pradyumna married Rukmī's daughter [Rukmavatī], who gave birth to Aniruddha. He was as strong as ten thousand elephants.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    He was a great warrior because he abducted Rukmavatī in a battle, defeating other kings. Aniruddha was stronger than Pradyumna. They followed pastimes in this world. Actually however they were all īśvara (supremely powerful).

    Important Words
    • vajraḥ — Vajra
      Sanskrit vajra — thunderbolt, diamond. The grandson of Aniruddha bears the name of Indra's weapon and the symbol of indestructibility. The naming is prophetic: of his entire generation, Vajra alone is vajra-hard enough to survive.
    • mauṣalāt — from the iron clubs episode
      Ablative of mauṣala — pertaining to the muṣala (iron club). The episode in SB 11.30 where the Yadus kill one another with iron clubs grown from the cursed pestle. Verse 90.37's single word anticipates the entire mausala-līlā.
    • avaśeṣitaḥ — remaining
      Past participle of ava + √śiṣ — to leave as remainder. Vajra is the remainder, the residue of the Yadu fire. Vaiṣṇava lineage continues through such residues — the few who survive carry the line forward.
    • pautrīm — the granddaughter
      Accusative of pautrī — son's daughter. Aniruddha's marriage to his father's wife's brother's son's daughter — Sanskrit kinship intricacy. The Bhāgavatam preserves the lineage even in dense detail.
    Rukmī’s daughter’s son [Aniruddha] married Rukmī’s son’s daughter [Rocana]. From her was born Vajra, who would remain among the few survivors of the Yadus’ battle with clubs.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Rukmī's daughter's son [Aniruddha] married Rukmī's son's daughter [Rocana]. From her was born Vajra, who would remain among the few survivors of the Yadus' battle with clubs.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Not only did Pradyumna marry his cousin, but Aniruddha also did. That is indicated by the word api. Aniruddha married Rukmi’s granddaughter. From Aniruddha (tataḥ) came Vajra.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Not only did Pradyumna marry his cousin, but Aniruddha also did. That is indicated by the word api. Aniruddha married Rukmi’s granddaughter. Or though shet was his granddaughter, it was unsuitable for her to marry Aniruddha because Rukmi hated Kṛṣṇa. The story was previously told. From Aniruddha (tataḥ) Vajra came. He alone remained, protected by the Lord, as the remnants of the dynasty, after the destruction from battle caused by the pestle. Though the story is not happy, this is mentioned to glorify the Lord.

    Concepts
    Jiva
    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    Aniruddha marries his great-uncle Rukmī's son's daughter Rocanā; their son Vajra would survive the mausala-līlā. The Bhāgavatam plants the seed of canto 11's catastrophe here in canto 10's closing chapter — Vajra alone of this generation will outlast the Yadus' fall.

    Stories
    Vajra and the mausala-līlā

    In SB 11.30-31 the Yadu dynasty self-destructs near Prabhāsa-tīrtha in a drunken brawl — sage's curse fulfilled. Of the dynasty, only a handful survive; Vajra is chief among them. Arjuna escorts him to Indraprastha and installs him at Mathurā as the heir of the Yadu line.

    Verse 90.37 quietly identifies him: 'who would remain among the few survivors of the Yadus' battle with clubs.' Gauḍīyas read this anticipation as Bhāgavatam's structural irony — Canto 10 ends bright, but the verse already names the survivor of the coming end.

    Important Words
    • prati-bāhuḥ — Pratibāhu
      prati (against, response) + bāhu (arm). 'Counter-arm' — a name suggesting martial readiness. The Yadu line preserves the warrior-quality of its founder. Gauḍīyas note: even at the dynasty's wind-down, the names announce dharma's defensive function.
    • subāhuḥ — Subāhu
      su (good, beautiful) + bāhu (arm). 'Beautiful-armed.' The Yadu naming alternates between martial vigor (Pratibāhu, Śāntasena, Śatasena) and aesthetic refinement (Subāhu). The dynasty preserves both.
    • śānta-senaḥ — Śāntasena
      Compound: śānta (peaceful) + sena (army). 'Of peaceful army' — the apparent paradox of Vaiṣṇava military: an army that brings peace. Compare Kṛṣṇa Himself, the supreme warrior whose battles install dharma.
    • ātma-jaḥ — son
      ātma (self) + ja (born). 'Self-born' — son in the natural sense. Each generation here is ātma-ja — proper succession, no adoption. Vaiṣṇava lineage continues by birth as well as by initiation.
    From Vajra came Pratibāhu, whose son was Subāhu. Subāhu’s son was Śāntasena, from whom Śatasena was born.

    Important Words
    • abrahmaṇyāḥ — neglectful of brāhminical culture
      a + brahmaṇya — un-Brahminical. The Yadus produced no one un-brāhminical. Gauḍīyas: brāhmaṇya in Vaiṣṇava reading is not caste but qualification — sevā, satya, dama. Kṛṣṇa's family upheld this universally.
    • alpa-āyuṣaḥ — short-lived
      alpa (little) + āyus (lifespan). No Yadu was short-lived. Long life in Vaiṣṇava reckoning is a fruit of dharma — and a longer field for bhakti's practice. The dynasty's longevity is itself a piece of bhakti's accumulation.
    • adhanaḥ — without wealth
      a + dhana — without riches. No Yadu was destitute. Gauḍīyas read this not as praise of mundane wealth but as a sign of dharmic balance: artha rightly subordinated to dharma is naturally abundant.
    • vīryāḥ — valor
      Plural of vīrya — potency, strength. The dynasty was full of vīrya. Gauḍīya theology: Bhagavān's family expresses His vibhūti through their progeny — vīrya is a divine inheritance, not a personal achievement.
    No one born in this family was poor in wealth or progeny, short-lived, weak or neglectful of brahminical culture.

    No one born in this family was poor in wealth or progeny, short-lived, weak or neglectful of brahminical culture.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    In the family of the Lord (etasmin) no one was born without wealth as the long as the mother and father were pure kṣatriyas.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Everyone else born in the family, besides those mentioned such as Vraja, had similar greatness. Not anyone (hi) born in the family of the Yādavas, related to the Lord, was lacking in wealth etc. Or none of them was lacking even in wealth etc.

    Important Words
    • vikhyāta-karmaṇām — of those of famous deeds
      Compound: vi + khyāta (widely known) + karman (deed). The Yadus' karmas are vikhyāta — broadcast. Vaiṣṇava karma is by definition broadcastable; secret virtue is incomplete (Caitanya-caritāmṛta: prema cannot be hidden).
    • saṅkhyā — enumeration
      From sam + √khyā — to count. The verse confesses the impossibility of saṅkhyā. Same word as Sāṅkhya philosophy (enumeration of categories). Bhāgavatam admits: where Bhagavān multiplies, philosophy's count fails.
    • yadu-vaṁśa-prasūtānām — of those born in the Yadu dynasty
      Triple compound: yadu + vaṁśa (lineage) + prasūta (brought forth). Birth in the Yadu line is itself an honor. Gauḍīya hagiography records that some Vaiṣṇava ācāryas were Yadus reincarnated — the line remains alive.
    • ayutaiḥ — by ten thousands
      Instrumental plural of ayuta (10,000). Sanskrit's standard large number. The verse uses it to denote years that fail at counting — a deliberate poetic crashing of arithmetic at the threshold of Bhagavān's family.
    The Yadu dynasty produced innumerable great men of famous deeds. Even in tens of thousands of years, O King, one could never count them all.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Yadu dynasty produced innumerable great men of famous deeds. Even in tens of thousands of years, O King, one could never count them all.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    One cannot enumerate even those who had the greatest prowess, what to speak of enumerating all the others. It is well known that the Yādava kings in Mathurā numbered fifty hundred and sixty billion.

    Stories
    Sāndīpani Muni teaching Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma, Sudāmā

    Earlier in this canto (SB 10.45) Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma went to Avantī to study under Sāndīpani Muni — completing the sixty-four arts in sixty-four days. Bhagavān submitted to a teacher's instruction, then offered guru-dakṣiṇā by retrieving the muni's drowned son from Saṁyamanī.

    Verse 90.41's 38.8 million ācāryas extend this pattern: Kṛṣṇa, who Himself sat at a guru's feet, ensures every Yādava child does the same. Gauḍīyas: even Bhagavān modeled gurukula; the dynasty inherits the discipline.

    Ugrasena .
    Important Words
    • āhukaḥ — Ugrasena (Āhuka)
      A patronymic of Ugrasena — Kaṁsa's father, Kṛṣṇa's maternal grandfather. Kṛṣṇa reinstalled him as king of Mathurā after slaying Kaṁsa. Gauḍīyas note: even those Bhagavān restores are restored at vast scale — Ugrasena's entourage is itself a small cosmos.
    • mahā-ātmanām — of the great souls
      Compound: mahā (great) + ātman (soul). Bhāgavata-vocabulary for Vaiṣṇavas of the highest order (Gītā 9.13: mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha). The Yādavas are addressed as mahātmās — not merely powerful, but spiritually great.
    • saṅkhyānam — enumeration
      Variant of saṅkhyā. Twice in two verses (40, 42) Bhāgavatam confesses enumeration fails. Aiśvarya cannot be tallied; the lover's bookkeeping breaks. Caitanya Mahāprabhu: kṛṣṇa-aiśvarya is anantam, beyond limit.
    • ayuta-lakṣeṇa — by a hundred million times ten thousand
      Compound: ayuta (10,000) + lakṣa (100,000). Three trillion: the multiplication of two large Sanskrit numbers. The poet pushes arithmetic past the speakable, the way mādhurya-rasa pushes intimacy past the displayable.
    Who can count all the great Yādavas, when among them King Ugrasena alone was accompanied by an entourage of thirty trillion attendants?
    Purport

    Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī explains why specifically thirty trillion, rather than an indefinite number of tens of trillions, is stated here to be the number of King Ugrasena’s attendants. He does so by citing the interpretational rule of kapiñjalādhikaraṇa, the logic of “referring to pigeons”: Somewhere in the Vedas is found the injunction that “one should sacrifice some pigeons.” This plural number should be taken to mean not an indiscriminate number of pigeons, but precisely three of them, since the Vedas never leave any matter vague. The rules of Mīmāṁsā interpretation take three as the default number when no specific number is given.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Who can count all the great Yādavas, when among them King Ugrasena alone was accompanied by an entourage of thirty trillion attendants?
    Commentary

    Ayutanam ayuta laksena means 3x 10,000 (ayuta) x 10,000 (ayuta) x 100,000 (laksa), or 30,000,000,000,000, or three sankhas. The description is in the present tense to express Sukadeva’s realization of the eternal nature of the pastimes.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    How can one count them all? One cannot count even the servants. Who can count the chief of the Yādavas? Among them Ugrasena had thirty trillion attendants. Instead of sa āhukaḥ sometimes sadāhukaḥ is seen. The present tense indicates the eternal pastimes. This will be established later.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    How can one count them all? One cannot count even the servants. Who can count the chief of the Yādavas? Because they were all devotees of the Lord, fully dedicated in their hearts, something will be said. Among them Ugrasena (āhukaḥ) had ten trillion attendants, or more.

    Important Words
    • daiteyāḥ — the descendants of Diti, demons
      From Diti, mother of asuras. The Bhāgavatam distinguishes daiteyas (Diti's line) from daityas (broadly) and dānavas (Danu's line). 90.43 names the daiteyas specifically — Diti's reborn brood needs Kṛṣṇa's incarnation to absorb them.
    • deva-asura-āhava — battles between demigods and demons
      Triple compound: deva + asura + āhava (battle). The recurring cosmic war. Gauḍīyas: this war is the structural background of every avatāra-līlā. Even Bhagavān's pastoral pastimes occur against demonic pressure (Pūtanā, Aghāsura, Kaṁsa).
    • su-dāruṇāḥ — very dreadful
      su (intensive) + dāruṇa (cruel, dreadful). The verse refuses to soften the demonic; evil is named as evil. Gauḍīyas: bhakti is realistic about adharma. There is no 'all is one' equivalence with the asuric.
    • babādhire — they harassed
      Perfect of √bādh — to oppress. The same verb used of demons throughout Bhāgavatam (e.g. Hiraṇyakaśipu bādhati prajāḥ). Vaiṣṇava cosmology: the world is a place where dharma is bādhita — pressed upon — until Bhagavān descends.
    The savage descendants of Diti who had been killed in past ages in battles between the demigods and demons took birth among human beings and arrogantly harassed the general populace.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya

    The reason for the unlimited number of Yādavas is explained in two verses. The demons were fierce and proud. They harassed the population.

    Related values & verses
    Concepts
    Jiva
    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    Demons killed in past wars between gods and asuras took human birth and harassed the people. The cosmic enemy never simply dies; it reincarnates. Bhagavān's descent is not luxurious; it is the response demanded by recurrent evil.

    Stories
    Hiraṇyakaśipu and Hiraṇyākṣa as Jaya and Vijaya

    Bhāgavatam (SB 3.16, 7.1) records that the gatekeepers of Vaikuṇṭha, Jaya and Vijaya, cursed by the four Kumāras, fell three times to take demoniac births so that the Lord could repeatedly kill and liberate them — first as Hiraṇyakaśipu/Hiraṇyākṣa, then as Rāvaṇa/Kumbhakarṇa, then as Śiśupāla/Dantavakra.

    Verse 90.43 frames the pattern more broadly: demons reborn as humans must be slain again. Gauḍīyas: this is why Bhagavān descends. Mokṣa for the demon is given through His weapon; protection for His devotees is given through the same act.

    Important Words
    • hariṇā — by Hari
      Instrumental of Hari — the Lord who removes (√hṛ). Bhagavān is the agent commanding the descent of the devas. In Gauḍīya theology, Hari is Kṛṣṇa's name as remover of all that obstructs bhakti — and of demons that obstruct dharma.
    • avatīrṇāḥ — descended
      Past participle of ava + √tṛ — to cross down. The technical verb for avatāra. Verse 90.44 confirms: the Yadu clansmen are themselves devas avatīrṇa — descended demigods. The Yadu line is a divine task-force.
    • yadoḥ kule — in the dynasty of Yadu
      yadoḥ (of Yadu, ancient ancestor) + kule (in the family). Yadu was Yayāti's son who declined the throne for tapas — Bhagavān honored him by descending in his line. Vaiṣṇava lineage rewards renunciation generations later.
    • nigrahāya — for subduing
      Dative of nigraha — restraint, suppression. The purpose of the Yadu descent is nigraha of demons. Gauḍīyas: avatāra is not theological luxury; it is dharma-rakṣaṇa — the structural answer to evil's persistence.
    To subdue these demons, Lord Hari told the demigods to descend into the dynasty of Yadu. They comprised 101 clans, O King.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    To subdue these demons, Lord Hari told the demigods to descend into the dynasty of Yadu. They comprised 101 clans, O King.
    Commentary

    The demigods formed a hundred and one clans, not individuals, since the number of individuals was countless.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    To control the demons the Lord told the devatās to appear in the Yadu dynasty. Sometimes the Lord killed the demons and sometimes he did it along with the devatās (as Yadus). Some entered into bodies of Yadu members and some were born separately as Yadus. Since they were in 101 clans, they are impossible to count.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The Lord told them to take birth in the Yadu dynasty to relieve the earth of its burden, by killing them. The family had 101 branches, with Bhogas, Andhakas, Sātvatas etc. Thus the dynasty was huge. Who can count the numbers? O king! By your intelligence you can determine this.

    Hari instructs the demigods to descend into the Yadu line — 101 clans strong — to subdue the reborn demons. The Yadu dynasty is not an accident; it is divine deployment. Aiśvarya is organized for adharma's defeat.

    Important Words
    • pramāṇam — the authority, the standard
      From pra + √mā — to measure. Hari is pramāṇa — the measure of right and wrong. Vedānta-vocabulary: śāstra is pramāṇa, guru is pramāṇa; here Bhagavān Himself is pramāṇa, source of all measures.
    • anuvartinaḥ — those who followed Him
      From anu + √vṛt — to follow, obey. Anuvartana is bhakti's behavior — to follow the Lord's path. Gauḍīyas: anugatya — being subordinate, following — is the structure of all sevā. Verse 90.45 names anuvartinaḥ as the flourishing ones.
    • vavṛdhuḥ — they flourished
      Perfect of √vṛdh — to grow. Vaiṣṇava growth is theological — bhakti grows the bhakta in every dimension. Caitanya-caritāmṛta 1.7.84: kṛṣṇa-bhakti śīghra-pradāyī — the followers of Hari grow rapidly toward His goal.
    • bhagavān — the Supreme Personality of Godhead
      From bhaga — fullness, opulence, glory. Six bhagas (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 6.5.74) define bhagavān: full power, fame, wealth, beauty, knowledge, renunciation. Gauḍīyas: bhagavān is the highest of three realizations (brahman, paramātmā, bhagavān).
    Because Lord Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Yādavas accepted Him as their ultimate authority. And among them, all those who were His intimate associates especially flourished.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Because Lord Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the Yādavas accepted Him as their ultimate authority. And among them, all those who were His intimate associates especially flourished.
    Commentary

    Those who were his eternal associates (anuvartinah), all in the form of Yadavas, increased the numbers of Yadus. The Lord alone could count their number because of their numbers, because such counting was beyond the abilities of Brahma and others.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Only the Lord knows how many eternal associates were present. Their number was even greater than those who were not eternal associates. All the Yādavas who were eternal associates of the Lord increased unlimitedly in powers and wealth. Only the Lord could bear witness to the amount of powers they had. Others could not. It was beyond the intelligence of Brahmā what to speak of the devatās. Hari-vaṁśa says devānāṁ ca hitārthāya vayaṁ yātā manuṣyatām: to help the devatās we came as humans. The Lord (hariḥ) has the power to bring everyone—eternal associates and others—together since he is endowed with his six qualities (bhagavān). That is the significance of hariḥ and bhagavān in this verse.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The unlimited number has been stated. Now their special glory is described in two verses. The Lord was the proof—that which produces faith--or the eternal goal for the unlimited Yadus, by his powers (prabhutvena). He was their power, since he manifested unlimited powers (bhagavān) and destroyed all faults and sorrow (hariḥ). But all the Yadus, dedicated to service in prema (anuvarinaḥ), increased in qualities and form etc. more than all others. Or their unlimited numbers though impossible because of the extraordinary power, should be believed. The Lord alone and no one else was the witness with his power, correct behavior etc. People cannot believe in the most extraordinary events. But they should believe. All the Yadus increased more than all others, since they were the Lord’s devotees (anuvartinaḥ).

    All the Yādavas accepted Hari as their ultimate authority — and His intimate associates among them especially flourished. Proximity to Bhagavān, lived as discipleship, is the engine of vṛddhi. Bhakti is not invisibly fertile; it makes its line grow.

    Stories
    Akrūra and the Syamantaka jewel

    In SB 10.57, Akrūra — one of Kṛṣṇa's most senior Yādava associates — went into exile during the Syamantaka-jewel controversy, and the kingdom was struck by drought. When Kṛṣṇa called him back, rains returned. The land followed the devotee's presence.

    Verse 90.45's claim — 'those who were His intimate associates especially flourished' — finds concrete narrative weight here. Gauḍīyas: a devotee is a center of prosperity for the surrounding region; Vaiṣṇava-saṅga is materially fertile and spiritually decisive.

    Important Words
    • kṛṣṇa-cetasaḥ — whose consciousness was on Kṛṣṇa
      Compound: kṛṣṇa + cetas (consciousness). The single technical term Prabhupāda translated as 'Kṛṣṇa-consciousness.' Verse 90.46 is one of its scriptural anchors. Not generic awareness, but consciousness whose object is Kṛṣṇa.
    • na viduḥ — they did not know
      Perfect of √vid — to know — with negation. They did not know — were unaware of — their own bodies. Bhakti reaches the level where viṣaya-consciousness lapses. Compare Gītā 6.7-9's samādhi vocabulary, transposed into rasa.
    • ātmānam — themselves, their own bodies
      Accusative of ātman. Critically: here ātman means body, not soul. Gauḍīyas note: the Vṛṣṇis did not forget themselves as eternal servants; they forgot the bodily ātman in absorption. The svarūpa-ātman is what remembers.
    • śayyā-āsana-aṭana-ālāpa-krīḍa-snāna-ādi-karmasu — in such activities as sleeping, sitting, walking, conversing, playing, bathing
      Long compound listing six everyday activities. Bhakti is not a special-time activity; it permeates the ordinary. Compare Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu 1.2.255: yat tava lakṣaṇaṁ rāgānugā — the rāgānugā-bhakta lives every breath in Kṛṣṇa's līlā.
    The Vṛṣṇis were so absorbed in Kṛṣṇa consciousness that they forgot their own bodies while sleeping, sitting, walking, conversing, playing, bathing and so on.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Vṛṣṇis were so absorbed in Kṛṣṇa consciousness that they forgot their own bodies while sleeping, sitting, walking, conversing, playing, bathing and so on.
    Commentary

    Summarizing the tenth canto, the ocean of Krsna’s eternal pastimes, Sukadeva speaks of five unique qualities of Krsna distinguishing him from other avataras. The holy place in the form of the glories of Krsna who was now born in the Yadu family made his foot water in the form of the Ganga insignificant. Previously the Ganga was superior to all purifying tirthas, but with the appearance of krsna, his glories became the supreme purifying tirtha. This is one remarkable fact. His enemies such as Kamsa and his devotees such as the gopis, attained respectively, sayujya or merging, and the form of the Lord with which they enjoyed pastimes (svarupam). This the second remarkable fact. Laksmi, whose mercy all others such as Brahma strive for, was unable to conquer him (ajita para). Even by severe austerities she could bring him under control and enjoy the rasa lila as the women of Vraja did. This is the third wonder. His name of two syllables, superior to all other names such as Narayana, which are portions of his name, destroys all inauspiciousness, even up to ignorance, the root of the material world. Or, that name eradicates all ignorance of his supreme position, thus capturing even the liberated souls. Recitation of that name overturns by his own excellence all attractive results of other sadhanas (sruti matha gaditam). This indicates the superior of the name of Krsna over other names such as Narayana which are its expansions. "One gains the result of chanting Visnu’s thousand names three times by chanting Krsna’s name once." This is a statement from the Brahmanda purana. This is the fourth wonder. He freed the whole earth (go trayate), going everywhere and protecting the earth with the four legs of dharma. At the end of dvapara yuga, dharma was lacking three legs. Krsna restored all four legs (gotra dharma). The earth said, "Once you too were maintained by your four legs, and you increased happiness all over the universe by the mercy of the Lord." Sb 1.16.25 This is the fifth wonder. With these five outstanding wonders of Krsna, his removing the burden of the earth is not at all astonishing, though it may be for the common man.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The greatest quality of the Yādavas is described. They were not aware of themselves while sleeping etc. and even while awake. They did everything under the inspiration of the Lord. They did not have the ability to individually investigate things since they were absorbed in Kṛṣṇa. Playing indicates playing dice. Ādi means even during amorous actions. Nothing could compare with this family. Yad yādavaṁ kulam aho aviṣahyam āste: the Yādava dynasty’s strength is unbearable for the earth. (SB 11.1.3) Kṛṣṇa however had fear of the state of madness that separation from him would cause them. This will be explained. brahmaṇyānāṁ vadānyānāṁ nityaṁ vṛddhopasevinām vipra-śāpaḥ katham abhūd vṛṣṇīnāṁ kṛṣṇa-cetasām How could the brāhmaṇas curse the Vṛṣṇis, who were always respectful to the brāhmaṇas, charitable, and inclined to serve senior and exalted personalities and whose minds were always fully absorbed in thought of Kṛṣṇa? SB 11.1.8

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The Yadus could not know themselves,. They did not examine what action and where, while existing (santam) in sleep, sitting, walking, conversing, playing or bathing, or any activity, because their minds were absorbed in Kṛṣṇa who attracts all hearts. Ādi indicates amorous acts also. This proves that their greatness is superior to great sages by their absorption in the Lord, even while having the great fortune of being directly in the presence of many attractive objects.

    Related values & verses
    Related values
    Vairagya (Detachment / Dispassion)Discriminative WisdomAbhaya (Fearlessness)Seva (Service / Selfless Action)Saurya (Heroism / Bravery)Samata (Equanimity / Even-mindedness)
    Related verses
    BG 2.60 BG 5.7 BG 12.5 BG 5.4 BG 16.2 BG 6.1 BG 9.26 BG 10.4 BG 3.27 BG 3.11 BG 18.1 BG 3.1
    Concepts
    KarmaLila
    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    The Vṛṣṇis were so absorbed in Kṛṣṇa-consciousness that even while sleeping, sitting, walking, conversing, playing, bathing — they forgot their own bodies. Phala-śruti begins: this is what the chapter has been about. Bhakti is the body's forgetfulness in the Beloved's remembrance.

    Stories
    Caitanya Mahāprabhu's body-forgetting

    Caitanya-caritāmṛta records that Mahāprabhu, especially in His Purī years, regularly forgot His body — losing track of meals, of clothing, of distance. Once at Tota-Gopinatha He walked into the sea, mistaking it for Yamunā; the fishermen pulled Him out unconscious.

    Gauḍīyas treat 90.46 as the technical description of this state — kṛṣṇa-cetasaḥ. The Vṛṣṇis lived continuously in what Mahāprabhu entered intermittently. The verse is read as the goal of sādhana: not body-suppression, but body-forgetting through full absorption.
